dedupe_keys.name: global opportunity areas for nature based solutions to reduce risks to infrastructure

description: This dataset maps where nature-based solutions, in the form of viable tree planting, could reduce risk to road and rail infrastructure through coastal erosion control, landslide risk reduction and river flood reduction, with global coverage at 250 m resolution (9 arc-second rasters). It gives opportunity areas for mangrove restoration classed by shoreline dynamics (accreting, static to slowly retreating, fast retreating), for slope revegetation on non-woodland slopes of 8 to 36 degrees classed by current land use (other, crops, bare ground), and for catchment planting in flood-prone sub-basins, together with native planting and mangrove costs in 2020 US dollars per hectare, a relative biodiversity benefit from the Biodiversity Habitat Index, additional carbon after a nominal 50 years, and baseline expected annual damage to roads and rail from landslides, river flooding and coastal flooding. Version 1.0.0 was published on 10 March 2025 by Tom Harwood and Tom Russell of the University of Oxford and is accessible as a free download of 22 files (GeoTIFF, GeoPackage, GeoParquet and CSV, about 24.5 GB) from Zenodo under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: the authors target initial screening only, fine-scale accuracy is limited by global inputs, and downstream effects outside a catchment are not modelled. It supports hazard exposure screening and appraisal of green infrastructure for climate adaptation of transport networks; related records are GIRI and open-gira.
